Great news! The **2026 NBA Finals** are currently underway, with the **New York Knicks vs. San Antonio Spurs**. Game 1 was on June 3, Game 2 on June 5, Game 3 on June 8, and Game 4 on June 10 — all on ABC at 8:30 p.m. ET.

Here are the best places to get tickets:

### 🎟️ Official Sources
- **[NBA.com](https://www.nba.com/schedule)** – Check the official schedule and ticket links directly on the NBA website.
- **[Ticketmaster](https://www.ticketmaster.com/nba)** – Ticketmaster is the Official Ticketing Partner of the NBA, and if tickets for a game are sold out, additional seats may become available closer to the game, so keep checking back.

### 🎟️ Resale Marketplaces
- **[SeatGeek](https://seatgeek.com/nba-finals-tickets)** – SeatGeek offers mobile entry for all NBA Finals events, making it simple to scan your tickets straight from your phone — no need to print anything.
- **[Vivid Seats](https://www.vividseats.com/nba-finals-tickets--sports-nba-basketball/performer/2724)** – All NBA Finals tickets are backed by their 100% Buyer Guarantee.
- **[nbatickets.us](https://nbatickets.us/)** – Offers tickets and VIP packages for current and upcoming games.

### 💰 Pricing
Ticket prices for NBA games depend on a variety of factors, including date and time, city, matchup, seat location, and when the tickets are purchased. The average ticket for an NBA game can cost anywhere between $100–$200. However, for the NBA Finals, prices will be significantly higher.

### 📅 Upcoming NBA Finals Games
Upcoming scheduled games include:
- **Game 5** – June 13 (New York at San Antonio, if necessary)
- **Game 6** – June 16 (San Antonio at New York, if necessary)
- **Game 7** – June 19 (New York at San Antonio, if necessary)

Be sure to act fast, as Finals tickets are in very high demand! Would you like help finding tickets for a specific team or location?
